newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil July industry sales up 5.91 pct vs June - CNI.
newsitem.headline: Brazil July industry sales up 5.91 pct vs June - CNI.

text.p: Sales by Brazilian industry in July were up a seasonally adjusted 5.91 percent from June, the private National Industry Confederation (CNI) said.
The result represents the single largest monthly increase since the CNI began recording industry sales in 1992, it said in a statement.
The CNI said July's sales were 14.94 percent higher than in the same month last year, reflecting in part the low levels of economic activity in July 1995.

Industry sales between January and July were 1.47 percent higher than during the same period last year, the first time in 1996 that accumulated sales have topped last year's comparative levels, the statement said.
"With the latest results, the manufacturing industry's activity reaches levels similar to those of the strongest production following (the introduction) of the Real (currency)," the CNI said.
A non-seasonally adjusted reading of industry sales in July showed an 8.05 percent increase from June, it said.
Hours worked rose a seasonally adjusted 4.07 percent from June, but were 7.4 percent lower than in July last year, reflecting lower employment in industry, it said.

Industry worked at a seasonally adjusted rate of 79 percent of capacity, compared with 77 percent in June and 77.3 percent in July 1995. In seasonally adjusted terms, the capacity rate in July was the highest since April 1995.
Employment in industry fell 0.16 percent in July from June, the smallest drop since job levels began falling in May 1995.
The slowing of that rate "indicates the possible end to the depressive side-effects on the industrial labor market where long-term trends now dominate," the statement said.
Industrial job levels were 8.2 percent lower in July than during the same month last year.
